rename.resolution: Not a rename. W1 moved our name off this key and W4 put the CAPABILITY back under it, which is the outcome the gap asked for.

why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-05 (phase-425 W4), gap -> divergence: the gap W1 opened is closed. `nros::create_timer(Node&, Timer&, const Clock&, std::chrono::milliseconds, std::function<void()>)` existed at `std_compat.hpp:83` in the since-DELETED header, the clock-taking counterpart of `nros::create_wall_timer` beside it, and the report now matches it under the systematic `no-shared-ptr` rule.

What differs is shape, and it is the same constraint the whole C++ timer family carries: a caller-owned `Timer&` instead of a returned `shared_ptr` (no allocator), and a `Node&` instead of rclcpp's `NodeT` / `shared_ptr<NodeBaseInterface> + shared_ptr<NodeTimersInterface>` pair — RFC-0002 puts one executor per RTOS task and there is no interface-fragment layer to pass.

The CAPABILITY is what mattered, and it is real rather than nominal: a `RCL_ROS_TIME` clock makes the timer advance with `/clock`, so it stops while a simulator is paused and tracks a bag's replay rate (`executor::arena::TimerClockSource`).

phase-427 W9 rebase (2026-09-09) -- DISPOSITION added, no re-verdict. `--require-disposition`'s second set (`same_shaped_divergences`) reached this row for the first time here, and the reason is a change on `main`, not in this branch: phase-430 W6 landed `rclcpp::create_timer(node, clock, period, callback)` as a free function (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:855`, chrono overload `:882`), so on the PORTED-file surface the name now exists with upstream's argument order and a returned `shared_ptr`. A ported line therefore COMPILES and nothing states the envelope -- exactly the class the gate was widened for.

The value is MEASURED from that header rather than chosen: its own comment reads "the same ADOPT-BOUNDED trade `get_clock()` itself makes" (`:815`). THE ENVELOPE: the clock parameter is `nros::Clock*`, which is what `node->get_clock()` returns, where upstream takes `rclcpp::Clock::SharedPtr` (no allocator, RFC-0022); the period is truncated to MILLISECONDS (`:860`); Humble's optional trailing `group` parameter is not taken; and the return is `shared_ptr<nros::Timer>` (`rclcpp::TimerBase` is an alias of the flat `rclcpp::Timer`, `timer.hpp`, so this IS `TimerBase::SharedPtr`). The `divergence` verdict and its `why` above still describe the NATIVE `nros::create_timer` out-ref shape, which is unchanged.

phase-442 W2 (2026-09-11) — `std_compat.hpp` is DELETED, so any sentence above naming that header describes a spelling that no longer exists. It was a third orphaned vocabulary: free functions shadowing the `Node` methods a ported file calls, dead in every shipping configuration, and RFC-0096 removed the layer it belonged to. The always-available spelling is the method.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it. The envelope above lived in a `//` banner, which Doxygen does not attach to the function; it is now on `rclcpp::create_timer`'s own `///` comment. Line citations drift: the free function is no longer at `rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:855`/`:882`/`:860`/`:815` — read it by name (`rclcpp::create_timer`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp`).

phase-476 W2 (2026-10-05) — `rclcpp::create_timer` returns `nros::TimerHandle` (what `rclcpp::TimerBase::SharedPtr` names now) and is freestanding: the callable is held in the executor arena, not a `std::function` cell the node co-owned. The clock, millisecond and `group` parts of the envelope are unchanged.
